The 19-year-old logged 24 regular-season appearances for the Tar Heels, averaging 19.8 points, 9.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.4 blocks and 1.5 steals across 31.3 minutes per game. However, after suffering a fractured left hand during the Feb. 10 meeting with Miami, he subsequently sustained a broken right thumb in practice,…

5099752.h: Rupert and the 76ers agreed to a two-way contract Friday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
5099752.s: A 2023 second-round pick, Rupert split his time between Portland and Memphis last season. Across 64 regular-season games, he averaged 5.2 points, 2.9 rebounds and 1.1 assists.

5101761.h: Brown (ankle) will miss Tuesday's preseason game against the Hornets, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
5101761.s: Brown recently began taking contact in practices and continues to trend in the right direction. The rookie is expected to play at some point during the preseason, but it's unclear when. His next chance to play comes Thursday against the 76ers in another exhibition.

5101761.h: Brown (ankle) has progressed to taking some contact in practice and said Sunday that he's "starting to get to full speed," Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
5101761.s: Brown rolled his ankle a couple of weeks ago but is ramping up ahead of the preseason. It wouldn't be surprising if the Nets proceed with caution ahead of the regular season, though the rookie guard's first opportunity to suit up in the preseason will come Tuesday against Charlotte.

5101761.h: Brown (ankle) hasn't been cleared to practice with contact and remains without a timetable for a return, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
5101761.s: Brown suffered an ankle injury before the start of training camp, and while he's been able to get back on the court in a limited capacity, the team is taking a cautious approach to his rehab. "Yeah, as of right now they're just telling me you could get back to moving a little bit, really just trying to get the strengthening it back up," said Brown on Thursday. "I mean, I am back on the court moving. That's all I'm…

5101761.h: General manager Sean Marks said Monday that Brown rolled his ankle last week and will ramp up at the start of training camp, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
5101761.s: The team "doesn't expect him to miss considerable time," though Brown's status will be worth monitoring heading into the Nets' preseason opener against the Hornets on Tuesday, Oct. 6. The rookie guard was selected with the sixth overall pick this summer and is expected to take on a sizable role early in his career. Over 21 appearances (19 starts) at Louisville in 2025-26, he averaged 18.2 points, 4.7 assists, 3.3…

5101761.h: Brown (rest) is primed for a significant role ahead of his rookie season in 2026-27.
5101761.s: The Nets chose Brown with the No. 6 overall pick in this year's draft, so they likely have big plans in mind for the 20-year-old guard right away in 2026-27. Brown, who averaged 15.0 points, 4.0 assists, 1.2 steals and 2.2 three-pointers per game over four Summer League appearances, is lined up to share Brooklyn's starting backcourt with Egor Demin.

5104155.h: Coulibaly (heel) could continue to see significant minutes, though likely off the bench, after Washington's selection of AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
5104155.s: His defensive versatility and ability to guard multiple positions complement the team's offensive-minded players, giving him a relatively secure role entering 2026-27. The presence of additional perimeter talent may limit his scoring opportunities, but Coulibaly still projects as an important contributor capable of providing value through defensive statistics. During the 2025-26 regular season, he averaged 1.3…

5104157.h: Wembanyama believes he's in better shape this season, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio.
5104157.s: Head coach Mitch Johnson is also looking for more growth in Wembanyama as a playmaker, per Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News. Any rise in ballhandling duties would be a welcome addition for the superstar big man, who's already a candidate to go first overall in fantasy drafts this fall as the reigning Defensive Player of the Year.

5104157.h: Wembanyama signed a five-year, $252 million extension with the Spurs on Friday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
5104157.s: Wembanyama is officially set to remain with the Spurs for the foreseeable future after signing a maximum rookie-scale extension with a player option in the final year. He was eligible for the supermax but opted for the max, giving San Antonio added financial flexibility. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year is fresh off a dominant 2025-26 campaign in which he averaged 25.0 points, 11.5 rebounds, 3.1 assists,…

5105550.h: With Cameron Boozer, Karim Lopez (undisclosed) and Jerami Grant now in the mix, Jackson faces increased competition for playing time in the 2026-27 campaign.
5105550.s: The Grizzlies are expected to focus on developing their young talent this season, though Jackson still faces plenty of competition for minutes. Memphis drafted Boozer and Lopez in June before acquiring Grant in the Ja Morant deal later that month. Jackson has flashed potential throughout his time in the NBA, which the Grizzlies rewarded this summer by exercising his $2.4 million team option. The 21-year-old's…

5105550.h: The Grizzlies exercised Jackson's (knee) $2.4 million team option Monday, Jake Fischer of BleacherReport.com reports.
5105550.s: Jackson has shown flashes offensively but struggled to stay healthy and put everything together in his first three seasons. However, the Grizzlies are still believers in his long-term upside. Across 55 regular-season contests in 2025-26, he averaged 12.5 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.5 assists on 49.6 percent shooting from the field.

5105553.h: Phillips signed a training camp contract with the Rockets on Friday, Paul Garcia of The Spot Up Shot reports.
5105553.s: Phillips will join the Rockets for training camp and compete for a spot on the club's regular-season roster. The 22-year-old forward was traded from the Bulls to the Timberwolves ahead of last season's trade deadline, though Minnesota declined its $2.41 million team option on his contract for 2026-27. Over 48 regular-season appearances (two starts) in 2025-26, he averaged 2.9 points in 8.9 minutes per showing.

5105553.h: The Timberwolves are declining Phillips' $2.41 million team option for the 2026-27 season, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
5105553.s: Phillips spent the first two-and-a-half years of his NBA career with the Bulls before being traded to the Timberwolves in February. He served in a minor role off the bench for both teams and was limited to garbage-time minutes during Minnesota's playoff run. Once free agency officially begins, Phillips will have the opportunity to catch on with a team looking for depth on the wing.

5105623.h: Ware has a clearer path to playing time on the Bucks and should have a better opportunity to find firmer footing than he had with Miami, per Zach Kram of ESPN.
5105623.s: Ware flashed potential in his first two years in the Association with Miami, and he averaged 11.1 points, 9.0 rebounds, 1.9 combined steals-plus-blocks and 0.7 assists in 22.1 minutes per game across 77 regular-season appearances (34 starts) in 2025-26. The big man also shot an impressive 39.5 percent from downtown on 3.0 three-point tries per contest last season. He was dealt to Milwaukee as part of the Giannis…

5105623.h: The Heat traded Ware, Tyler Herro (foot), Jaime Jaquez, Kasparas Jakucionis, three first-round picks, one pick swap and one second-round pick to the Bucks on Monday in exchange for Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) and Bobby Portis (wrist), Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
5105623.s: After spending the first two seasons of his career in Miami, Ware will get a fresh start in Milwaukee. The 22-year-old center saw similar playing time in his second season compared to his first, though he still took a step forward in 2025-26. Over 77 regular-season appearances (34 starts) last season, the big man averaged 11.1 points, 9.0 rebounds, 1.1 blocks, 0.8 steals and 0.7 assists in 22.1 minutes per contest.…

5105637.h: Bona (foot) will not play in Monday's preseason opener against New York, Chris Hine of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
5105637.s: Bona has been sidelined by a foot sprain suffered during FIBA competition and has yet to practice during training camp. Coach Nick Nurse recently expressed optimism that Bona could return for a couple of Philadelphia's preseason contests, making his status worth monitoring over the coming days.

5105637.h: 76ers coach Nick Nurse said Bona (foot) will be re-evaluated in a couple days, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
5105637.s: Bona has been recovering from a foot sprain he suffered during the offseason. According to Nurse, there's a chance Bona could be back for a portion of the preseason. He is currently penciled in as Joel Embiid's backup for the upcoming season.

5105637.h: Bona (foot) will be re-evaluated at the start of training camp, Derek Bodner of AllPHLY.com reports.
5105637.s: Bona suffered a foot sprain this offseason, clouding his ability to participate in camp later this month. It's unclear if his status for Opening Night is in serious doubt, as he does have about a month until the regular season begins. Until Bona is cleared to retake the floor, Dominick Barlow and Ariel Hukporti should handle the backup center reps.

5105806.h: The Mavericks signed Howard to a two-way contract Monday.
5105806.s: Howard spent the first three years of his career with the Magic. Even though he averaged career-high marks in minutes (12.6) and points (5.5) per game in 55 regular-season contests in 2025-26, Howard was unable to do enough to stay in Orlando. Howard should compete for playing time at the NBA level, but if he doesn't stick around in Dallas, he should be a regular in the G League thanks to his two-way deal.

5105839.h: Sensabaugh won't play in Sunday's preseason opener against the Nuggets due to a left hip injury, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
5105839.s: Sensabaugh's absence from Sunday's exhibition seems largely precautionary. His next chance to play will come Tuesday in a rematch with the Nuggets.

5106060.h: Walker took another step forward during his third NBA season, earning a larger role in Indiana's rotation thanks to his defensive versatility and improving offensive game.
5106060.s: The 2023 lottery pick remains one of the Pacers' most intriguing young forwards and could continue seeing increased opportunities as his development progresses. He enters 2026-27 positioned to remain a key member of Indiana's frontcourt rotation.

5106258.h: Dick could see increased opportunities to begin the season while Brandon Ingram recovers from a partially torn Achilles and right heel surgery.
5106258.s: Dick arrived in Los Angeles alongside Ingram in the Kawhi Leonard trade and will compete for minutes on a Clippers team currently thin on the wing. Ingram's absence gives Dick an opportunity to earn a consistent rotation role, though he'll still face competition for playing time.

5106258.h: The Clippers and Raptors mutually agreed Monday to complete the trade sending Leonard to Toronto in exchange for Brandon Ingram (heel), Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, one first-round pick swap and two second-rounders, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
5106258.s: The trade hit a snag in July when the league investigated Leonard and the Clippers for salary cap circumvention, but the deal is now official ahead of training camp. The 2023 first-rounder is searching for a fresh start in Los Angeles after averaging 6.0 points and 1.9 rebounds in 14.0 minutes per game across 76 regular-season appearances (one start) for the Raptors last year.

5106258.h: The NBA has concluded its investigation into salary cap circumvention involving Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers, and the trade sending Dick to Los Angeles is expected to be finalized in the coming days, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
5106258.s: Among other punishments, the Clippers were stripped of five first-round picks Wednesday. Furthermore, Leonard was fined $700,000 in restitution for improper benefits. With the findings and penalities being announced, Dick is now expected to officially join the Clippers after spending his first three seasons in the Association with Toronto. The 2023 No. 13 overall pick's production took a hit in 2025-26, during which…

5106258.h: The Raptors are expected to send Dick, Brandon Ingram, two first-round picks, a first-round pick swap and two second-round picks to the Clippers on Tuesday in exchange for Kawhi Leonard, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
5106258.s: After a promising sophomore campaign, Dick took a major step back in Year 3 and will look for a fresh start with a change of scenery. The sharpshooter shot over 35 percent from three in each of his first two seasons but hit rock bottom in 2025-26, shooting 30.3 percent on 2.4 three-point attempts per game while playing only 14 minutes a night over 76 regular-season games. Dick will likely be competing with Kobe…

5107173.h: Wolf (rest) is ticketed for a reserve role in 2026-27 after the Nets acquired Julius Randle from Minnesota earlier this offseason.
5107173.s: Wolf closed last season as a starter while the Nets gradually began shutting down most of their key players, but the 2025 first-rounder might even struggle for a significant Opening Night role in 2026-27. Not only did Brooklyn add Randle as its starting power forward, but the team also signed Moritz Wagner and drafted Joshua Jefferson to further upgrade the frontcourt.

5107173.h: Wolf (rest) won't play in Sunday's Summer League game against the Thunder, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
5107173.s: Wolf will sit out Brooklyn's Summer League finale for rest purposes. The 22-year-old big man will finish the Las Vegas Summer League with averages of 11.8 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 0.8 steals and 0.8 blocks in 21.4 minutes per tilt across four outings.

5107173.h: Wolf (back) is out for Monday's California Classic Summer League Game against the Warriors Blue, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
5107173.s: Wolf will miss a third straight Summer League game due to lower-back soreness. His next opportunity to play comes Friday against the Knicks in Las Vegas.

5107173.h: Wolf (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's California Classic Summer League game against the Bucks, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
5107173.s: Wolf is dealing with lower-back soreness and will miss a second consecutive Summer League contest. His next opportunity to play will come Monday against the Kings.

5107173.h: Wolf didn't play in Saturday's 79-76 California Classic Summer League loss to the Kings due to lower-back soreness, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
5107173.s: Coach Dutch Gaitley said the Nets want to be smart about Wolf's availability in Summer League, and his next chance to play will come Sunday against the Bucks. The big man missed Brooklyn's final 11 regular-season games due to an ankle sprain, finishing the 2025-26 campaign with averages of 8.9 points, 4.9 rebounds and 2.2 assists across 20.8 minutes per contest in 57 regular-season games (15 starts).

5107897.h: Mogbo (rest) won't play in Tuesday's Summer League game against the Nets, Jason Anderson of The Sacramento Bee reports.
5107897.s: Mogbo will sit out the front end of this back-to-back set for rest purposes. His next opportunity to suit up in Las Vegas will come Wednesday against the Celtics.

5107897.h: Mogbo (undisclosed) is available and starting Thursday's Summer League game against the Clippers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
5107897.s: Mogbo didn't play in Monday's California Classic Summer League win over the Bucks, though he'll return to action Thursday. The 24-year-old forward signed a two-way pact with Sacramento earlier this month and will likely spend most of his time with the Kings' G League affiliate, the Stockton Kings, in 2026-27.

5107897.h: Mogbo will not play in Monday's California Classic Summer League game against the Bucks for undisclosed reasons, Sean Cunningham of Fox 40 Sacramento reports.
5107897.s: Mogbo played both games in the team's back-to-back set over the weekend and will get a night off for the third game in as many days. His next chance to suit up will come Thursday in the Las Vegas Summer League against the Clippers.

5107897.h: Mogbo will sign a two-way contract with the Kings, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports Wednesday.
5107897.s: Previously with the Raptors, Mogbo will become a developmental project for the Kings. Presumably, he will spend the bulk of his time in the G League early on. Mogbo made 40 regular-season appearances in 2025-26 for an average of 6.2 minutes per contest.

5107897.h: The Raptors declined their team option on Mogbo's contract for the 2026-27 campaign, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports Monday.
5107897.s: After spending the first two years of his career in Toronto, Mogbo will enter unrestricted free agency. The 24-year-old forward saw a significant decline in playing time in his second season, averaging 1.5 points and 1.7 rebounds in 6.2 minutes per game across 40 regular-season outings in 2025-26.

5112087.h: Wells faces competition for a starting spot on the wings in Memphis to begin the 2026-27 season, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
5112087.s: Jerami Grant, Cedric Coward and Cam Spencer are all competing with Wells for a starting spot on the wings. The 23-year-old swingman has started 143 of his 148 career regular-season appearances since being drafted by Memphis with the 39th overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, and he averaged 12.5 points, 3.2 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 0.9 steals in 26.4 minutes per contest across 69 regular-season games (all starts) in…

5112087.h: Wells (toe) has been a full participant during training camp, Grizzlies president of basketball operations Zach Kleiman said, according to Memphis reporter Landon Speck.
5112087.s: Wells has been cleared for full basketball activities after undergoing toe surgery in March and is practicing without restrictions during camp. His availability should give him plenty of time to ramp up during the preseason while competing for a prominent role on the wing.

5112087.h: Wells (toe) should continue competing for rotation minutes on the wing despite Memphis adding Cameron Boozer with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
5112087.s: Wells' defensive ability and complementary skill set could help him carve out a role alongside the Grizzlies' established core. However, increased competition for minutes may make consistent opportunities more difficult to secure. In addition to Boozer, the Grizzlies also added forward Karim Lopez in the first round.

5124612.h: Edgecombe said Monday that he placed an emphasis on improving his shooting during the offseason while also working on his finishing and ball-handling, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
5124612.s: Edgecombe established himself as a significant part of Philadelphia's rotation as a rookie, but improving his perimeter efficiency was an obvious area of focus heading into his second season. He shot 43.6 percent from the field and 35.9 percent from three across 79 regular-season appearances, and continued development as a shooter could make him an even more effective complement to the 76ers' other high-usage…

5124612.h: Edgecombe is not on the Bahamas' roster ahead of the FIBA World Cup qualifiers, according to NBA reporter Marc Stein.
5124612.s: There's no injury to report, and this is likely Edgecombe's decision. Presumably, his focus is going to be on ramping up ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season, when he'll look to build on a breakout rookie season. However, he'll face added competition for usage after the 76ers added LeBron James and Jaylen Brown this offseason.

5124612.h: Edgecombe could benefit from entering a veteran-laden environment after Philadelphia added LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Paul Hudrick of Liberty Ballers reports.
5124612.s: While touches may be harder to come by, Edgecombe will have less pressure to create offense immediately and should continue developing alongside one of the league's deepest rosters. Across 75 regular-season games in 2025-26, Edgecombe averaged 16.0 points, 5.6 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 1.4 steals.

5142620.h: Acuff is projected to open the season as Sacramento's starting point guard, according to Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140.
5142620.s: Nunes views Acuff, Zach LaVine, Keegan Murray, De'Andre Hunter and Domantas Sabonis as the Kings' most likely starting five. If Acuff secures the starting job, the rookie should have an opportunity to handle significant minutes and playmaking responsibilities from the outset. Efficiency could be an issue early on given the learning curve at the position.

5142620.h: Acuff enters his rookie season with an opportunity to earn developmental minutes in Sacramento's backcourt after being selected in the first round of the 2026 NBA Draft.
5142620.s: The dynamic scoring guard could spend time learning behind the Kings' veteran guards while adjusting to the NBA game, but a starting role on Opening Night could be on the table. Acuff's long-term upside as a shot creator makes him one of Sacramento's top young prospects.

5142620.h: Acuff will be rested for Friday's Summer League game against the Hornets, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
5142620.s: Acuff will be rested for a second straight exhibition. The rookie made five appearances during Summer League play, posting averages of 19.2 points, 4.6 assists and 1.6 rebounds.

5142620.h: Acuff will be rested for Wednesday's Summer League game against the Celtics, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
5142620.s: The Kings will also rest Nique Clifford and Maxime Raynaud during the second leg of this back-to-back set. It remains to be seen if Acuff will suit up for Friday's exhibition against Charlotte. Acuff produced 26 points (9-18 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five assists, one steal and one block over 26 minutes during Tuesday's 115-83 Las Vegas Summer League loss to the Nets.

5142620.h: Acuff (undisclosed) is available for Monday's California Classic Summer League game versus the Bucks, Sean Cunningham of Fox 40 Sacramento reports.
5142620.s: Acuff returns after a one-game absence and should resume his role as a starter. With Acuff back in the mix, Isaiah Stevens will likely head back to the second unit and Marquel Sutton is likely to see a minutes reduction.

5142718.h: Dybantsa (rest) will be competing for a starting role during training camp this fall.
5142718.s: After Dybantsa went first overall in the 2026 NBA Draft, there's a good chance the Wizards will want to showcase him in the first unit immediately. That said, Bilal Coulibaly was a full-time starter a year ago, and Washington also has incumbent veteran Khris Middleton on the roster. Regardless, Dybantsa finds himself in a rather favorable situation playing alongside veteran stars Trae Young (quad) and Anthony Davis…

5142718.h: The Wizards are shutting down Dybantsa (rest) for the team's final three Summer League games, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
5142718.s: Dybantsa was able to make a pair of Las Vegas Summer League appearances before being shut down. The 2026 No. 1 overall pick will now set his sights toward training camp in the fall ahead of his highly anticipated rookie campaign in 2026-27.

5142718.h: Dybantsa was selected by the Wizards with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
5142718.s: Dybantsa has been on the national stage since his freshman year of high school, when he earned Massachusetts Gatorade Player of the Year honors. The 19-year-old forward is coming off an impressive freshman campaign at BYU, where he led Division I basketball in scoring and averaged 25.5 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.1 steals while shooting 51.0 percent from the field and 33.1 percent from deep in 34.8…

5144091.h: Fears is set to share the second unit with Bennedict Mathurin in 2026-27.
5144091.s: The Pelicans bolstered their bench with Wednesday's signing of Mathurin, who is expected to help lead New Orleans' second unit alongside Fears in the backcourt. Over 82 regular-season games in 2025-26, Fears averaged 14.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.4 assists in 25.8 minutes per game.

5144091.h: Fears enjoyed an outstanding rookie season, appearing in all 82 regular-season games while averaging 14.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.4 assists.
5144091.s: Fears capped the year by setting the franchise rookie scoring record with a 40-point performance and enters 2026-27 as one of New Orleans' most promising young guards. Even with Dejounte Murray expected back, Fears has positioned himself for a significant role in the Pelicans' backcourt rotation.

5149077.h: Flemings will start Monday's preseason game against the Grizzlies, Kevin Chouinard of the Hawks' official site reports.
5149077.s: With CJ McCollum (nose) unavailable, Flemings will draw the start in his preseason debut. The rookie will be joined in the first unit by Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu.

5149077.h: Flemings enters his rookie season after Atlanta selected him with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
5149077.s: Hawks president of basketball operations Onsi Saleh praised Flemings' competitiveness on both ends of the floor following the draft, and the young guard should have an opportunity to earn minutes despite Atlanta's considerable perimeter depth. Flemings' immediate fantasy value will depend on how quickly he can carve out a role, but his draft capital makes him one of the organization's most important developmental…

5149077.h: Flemings (rest) won't play in Saturday's Summer League game against the Wizards, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
5149077.s: Flemings will sit out the Hawks' Summer League finale, marking his third consecutive contest on the inactive list. In two Las Vegas Summer League outings, he averaged 7.0 points, 6.5 assists, 4.0 rebounds and 1.5 combined steals-plus-blocks in 24.3 minutes per contest.

5149077.h: Flemings (rest) won't play in Thursday's game against the Grizzlies, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
5149077.s: Flemings played two games during the Salt Lake City Summer League before making two appearances in Las Vegas. The 2026 No. 8 overall pick wasn't consistently productive during those four contests, though it's evident the team is still comfortable keeping him off the floor.

5149077.h: Flemings (rest) is out for Monday's Summer League game against Boston, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
5149077.s: The Hawks are sitting multiple players for this exhibition. Flemings produced nine points (4-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt), seven rebounds, five assists and one block across 25 minutes in Saturday's 83-76 Summer League win over the Nets.

5160992.h: Sarr said he took part in the Wizards' 5-on-5 full-contact work during Monday's practice, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
5160992.s: Sarr is ramping up after undergoing right foot surgery in June. He appears likely to be ready for the start of the regular season, though it's unclear how much action he'll see during the preseason. Across 48 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, he averaged 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 2.0 blocks and 0.8 steals in 27.2 minutes per showing.

5160992.h: Sarr (foot) is expected to begin contact work soon after undergoing surgery this offseason, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
5160992.s: Sarr is nearing the next step in his recovery from surgery he underwent in mid-June to repair a fractured right foot. The Wizards planned to hold the big man out of contact drills during the first week of training camp, but he's expected to begin full-contact work soon. Sarr remains on track to be ready for the start of the regular season, though his availability for preseason action remains unclear.

5160992.h: Sarr (foot) didn't participate in Saturday's scrimmage but is expected to ramp up to full contact in the coming days, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
5160992.s: Sarr has been limited in training camp thus far while working his way back from surgery he underwent in mid-June to repair a fractured right foot. The big man is expected to be ready for the start of the regular season, though it's unclear how active he'll be during the preseason. Over 48 regular-season games in 2025-26, he averaged 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 2.0 blocks and 0.8 steals in 27.2 minutes…

5160992.h: Sarr will be a partial participant when training camp begins as he continues his recovery from surgery to repair a fractured right foot, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
5160992.s: General manager Will Dawkins said Thursday that Sarr is expected to be ready for the start of the regular season, so the limited workload to begin camp appears precautionary. Sarr underwent surgery in mid-June, and his progress during the preseason will be worth monitoring, but there currently doesn't appear to be significant concern about his availability for Opening Night.

5160992.h: Washington's selection of AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft likely won't significantly alter Sarr's (foot) role heading into his third NBA season.
5160992.s: The 21-year-old big man is currently recovering from foot surgery but is expected to be ready for training camp after averaging 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds and 2.0 blocks in 48 regular-season appearances last year. Sarr remains a major part of the franchise's long-term plans, although the additions of established veterans could reduce some offensive responsibilities. His defensive upside should continue to provide…

5164559.h: Ament (undisclosed) is in the starting lineup for Friday's Summer League game against the Heat, per Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel.
5164559.s: The Bucks held the rookie first-rounder out of California Classic Summer League play, but Ament is ready to roll Friday. He'll have a chance to showcase himself and play a featured role for as long as Milwaukee keeps him available this summer.

5164559.h: Ament (undisclosed) didn't play in Monday's 95-89 California Classic Summer League loss to the Kings.
5164559.s: The Bucks' trade with the Heat involving Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) and Ament was made official Monday, though the latter didn't suit up for Milwaukee in its California Classic finale. His next opportunity to make his Summer League debut will come in the Bucks' Las Vegas Summer League opener against the Heat on Friday.

5164559.h: Ament (undisclosed) didn't play in Saturday's 97-83 California Classic Summer League win over the Warriors or Sunday's 89-69 California Classic Summer League loss to the Nets.
5164559.s: Ament, Brayden Burries and Malique Lewis all sat out Milwaukee's first two games of the California Classic. It's unclear if any of the Bucks' rookies will play Monday against the Kings, though they'll likely be available for the Las Vegas Summer League, which starts Thursday, with the Bucks' first game coming Friday against the Heat.

5164559.h: Ament was selected by the Bucks with the No. 13 overall selection in the 2026 NBA Draft.
5164559.s: Ament appeared in 35 games for Tennessee in his lone college campaign, averaging 16.7 points, 6.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.6 blocks while shooting 39.9 percent from the field in 29.7 minutes per tilt. The 6-foot-10 forward earned Second-Team All-SEC and SEC All-Freshman Team honors for the Volunteers. Ament will be competing with Jaime Jaquez and Kyle Kuzma for minutes in Milwaukee, so it'll be…

5174563.h: George's (elbow) role becomes less certain after Washington added another high-upside wing prospect in AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
5174563.s: George displayed intriguing playmaking ability and positional versatility during his sophomore campaign. However, the Wizards now possess considerable depth on the wing, including fellow talented youngsters Tre Johnson and Bilal Coulibaly. George is currently penciled into the starting lineup, but his offensive opportunities may fluctuate depending on lineup combinations. The Wizards also just re-signed Trae Young…

5175643.h: Demin (rest) is looking to take a step forward ahead of his second NBA season in 2026-27.
5175643.s: The 2025 first-rounder is coming off an exciting Summer League run, having averaged 21.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.8 steals and 2.6 three-pointers per game over five appearances. Demin is set to work alongside a new backcourt partner after the Nets drafted Mikel Brown earlier this summer, and he should operate as a full-time starter in 2026-27.

5175643.h: Demin (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's Summer League game against the Thunder, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
5175643.s: Demin is healthy but will be inactive for the Nets' Summer League finale for rest purposes. The 20-year-old scored at least 20 points in all five of his Summer League appearances between the California Classic and Las Vegas. He figures to play a significant role in Brooklyn's backcourt during the 2026-27 campaign.

5175643.h: Demin (rest) won't play in Saturday's Summer League game against the Hawks, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
5175643.s: Demin will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set after dropping 20 points during Friday's win over the Knicks. His next chance to play will come Tuesday against the Kings.

5175643.h: Demin (undisclosed) has been ruled out for Sunday's California Classic Summer League game against Milwaukee, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
5175643.s: Demin underwent a foot procedure in March, though he was on the floor for Saturday's 79-76 Summer League loss to Sacramento. While he shot a rough 2-for-8 from downtown, he still led the Nets in scoring, finishing with 23 points across 24 minutes. Brooklyn's next Summer League game is Monday against Warriors Blue.

5175643.h: Demin (foot) could have more competition for playmaking opportunities at point guard after the Nets took Mikel Brown with the No. 6 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
5175643.s: Although Brooklyn employs a crowded backcourt, its long-term vision likely involves Demin and Brown coalescing in the guard spots. Demin dealt with plantar fasciitis in his left foot during his rookie season, limiting him to 52 regular-season appearances, but he's still lined up as the Nets' top point guard in 2026-27. Whether or not Brown or perhaps Drake Powell is starting alongside Demin remains to be seen,…

5175647.h: Gonzalez is looking to take a step forward in his second season, per Bobby Krivitsky of Forbes.com.
5175647.s: The door is open for Gonzalez to claim a larger role at training camp in the wake of Jaylen Brown's departure to Philadelphia. The camp battle between Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Sam Hauser will remain one for fantasy managers to keep tabs on this fall, though it's possible Boston will ultimately take a hot-hand approach with the three throughout the course of the year.

5175647.h: Gonzalez has a chance to claim a larger role in 2026-27 after the Celtics traded Jaylen Brown to the 76ers in exchange for Paul George.
5175647.s: Assuming Boston remains steadfast in keeping Payton Pritchard as its sixth man off the bench, the competition for the starting spot at shooting guard should come down to Gonzalez and Baylor Scheierman. Gonzalez made only three starts to Scheierman's 20 last regular season, so the former is likely to need a standout training camp this fall to make inroads in the race for a spot in the first unit.

5175647.h: Gonzalez (rest) won't play in Saturday's Summer League game against Orlando, John Karalis of BostonSportsJournal.com reports.
5175647.s: Gonzalez will sit out the Celtics' Summer League finale after dropping 24 points in Wednesday's win over the Kings. Over three Las Vegas Summer League appearances, he averaged 18.3 points, 8.0 rebounds, 5.7 assists and 1.7 steals in 34.7 minutes per tilt.

5175647.h: Gonzalez (rest) is sitting out Monday's Summer League game against the Hawks, per Jack Simone of BostonSportsJournal.com.
5175647.s: The Celtics appear to be holding Gonzalez out for maintenance reasons Monday. It's unclear if he'll make another appearance during the Las Vegas Summer League.

5175647.h: Gonzalez plans to play both FIBA qualifiers for Spain and in the Summer League for the Celtics, per Bobby Manning of Celtics on CLNS.
5175647.s: Gonzalez appears to be staying active this summer in preparation for his second NBA season in the fall. With Jaylen Brown's standing in Boston very much in limbo this offseason, Gonzalez could be thrust into a more significant role in 2026-27 if Brown is indeed traded away.

5175737.h: Lendeborg will start Golden State's preseason opener against the Clippers on Sunday, Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
5175737.s: Lendeborg appears to be in a position to take on a substantial role right from the start of the 2026-27 season, and the Warriors are eager to see what he can do alongside the likes of Stephen Curry and Brandin Podziemski. He figures to see his share of work during the preseason to prepare him for his first NBA campaign.

5175737.h: Head coach Steve Kerr said Monday that Lendeborg is "clearly going to play a ton," regardless of whether he starts or comes off the bench, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
5175737.s: The No. 11 overall pick in this year's draft, Lendeborg is fresh off winning a national championship with Michigan, where he averaged 15.1 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.2 blocks and 1.1 steals in 30.2 minutes per tilt across 40 games. He also earned Big Ten Player of the Year honors. The forward will be 24 years old when the season begins, and he'll seemingly step into a significant role right away for a…

5175737.h: Lendeborg is in the running to start this season, Monte Poole of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
5175737.s: "We've added some good players with Yaxel, Georges Niang, and believe Brandon Williams can help us," head coach Steve Kerr said during a recent interview. "The biggest things are figuring out who's going to start, and what's the rotation going to look like? Can Yaxel play the 3 with Draymond at the 4, with Kristaps or Al at the 5? What would that look like?" Lendeborg looked good during both the California Classic…

5175737.h: Lendeborg (undisclosed) is available and starting Thursday's Summer League game against the Mavericks.
5175737.s: Lendeborg was held out of Warriors Gold's California Classic loss to the Heat on Monday, though he'll return for the Warriors' Las Vegas Summer League opener. He'll be joined in the first unit by LJ Cryer, Will Richard, Graham Ike and Malevy Leons.

5175737.h: Lendeborg (undisclosed) won't play in Monday's California Classic Summer League game against the Heat, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
5175737.s: Monday marks the Warriors Gold's second game in as many nights, so Lendeborg will receive a rest day, which should open up minutes for Alex Toohey and Max Shulga. Lendeborg should return for the Warriors' first game in Las Vegas Summer League on Thursday.

5203685.h: The Suns exercised the team's third-year option for 2027-28 on Maluach on Thursday.
5203685.s: This was a no-brainer decision after Maluach was selected in the first round last year. The second-year big man could be primed to take on a significantly larger role in Phoenix's frontcourt, which has a major void due to Mark Williams' offseason shoulder injury, and the camp battle between Maluach and Oso Ighodaro for the top center spot could stretch all the way up until the end of the preseason.

5203685.h: Maluach earned significant praise from Devin Booker on Monday for the progress he's made during the offseason, Shane Young of the Suns' official site reports.
5203685.s: "I'd say he's taken the biggest leap of anyone I've seen this summer," Booker said of the second-year center. Maluach averaged just 8.9 minutes across 46 regular-season appearances as a rookie, but he followed that limited role with an impressive showing at Summer League. Booker's strong praise provides another encouraging sign that Maluach could be ready to take on a substantially larger role in Phoenix's…

5203685.h: The door is open for Maluach to start at center for the Suns in the wake of Mark Williams' offseason shoulder surgery, Bobby Marks of ESPN.com reports.
5203685.s: The 2025 first-rounder is coming off a promising Summer League run, averaging 19.5 points, 12.8 rebounds, 2.0 blocks and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 53.2 percent from the floor over four appearances. Williams is expected to miss around five months, so the runway with Phoenix's top spot at center could be a long one. Maluach does have Oso Ighodaro to overcome for the role, so fantasy managers should keep close…

5203685.h: Maluach is set to battle with Oso Ighodaro for the top backup role at center behind Mark Williams during training camp.
5203685.s: The 19-year-old big man put forth a dominant Summer League run, averaging 19.5 points, 12.8 rebounds, 2.0 blocks and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 53.2 percent from the field over four appearances. Ighodaro is the early favorite to handle the No. 2 center minutes behind Williams, though a strong showing at camp could force the Suns to give Maluach more consideration.

5203685.h: The Suns are shutting down Maluach (rest) for the rest of the Las Vegas Summer League, per John Gambadoro of Arizona Sports 98.7 FM.
5203685.s: Maluach put together an encouraging Las Vegas Summer League run, scoring at least 15 points in four appearances while registering three double-doubles as well. The 2025 first-rounder is next set to battle with Oso Ighodaro for the top backup role at center behind Mark Williams during training camp.

5211175.h: Risacher is adjusting well to his new team and is looking forward to playing alongside Cooper Flagg, Grant Afseth of the Dallas Sports Journal reports.
5211175.s: Risacher has been adjusting well after being traded from the Hawks to the Mavericks in July, and he noted Thursday that he's confident his style will mesh well with Flagg. "I feel like we're going to be a good fit, especially in this team. We're going to play fast. We want to go," said Risacher. "We're going to play physical, and I feel like that's going to be a good fit. I like to play off-ball too, so I feel like…

5211175.h: Risacher was traded to the Mavericks on Sunday as part of a three-team deal that sent Luguentz Dort and Ryan Nembhard (illness) to the Hawks and three second-round picks to the Thunder, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
5211175.s: After being selected No. 1 overall in the 2024 NBA Draft, Risacher's tenure in Atlanta comes to an end as he'll head to Dallas. In 67 regular-season games (46 starts) with the Hawks during the 2025-26 campaign, the wing averaged 9.6 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.1 assists in 22.4 minutes per contest. Risacher still has much to prove heading into his third NBA season and will likely slot into a reserve role with the…

5211175.h: The addition of Aaron Wiggins could further cut into Risacher's role during the 2026-27 season.
5211175.s: Risacher's minutes declined each month after January last season, and he was eventually demoted to the second unit after CJ McCollum solidified himself as a starter. Risacher was not a consistent part of the playoff rotation, and now he'll face even more competition for minutes following the arrival of Wiggins. The former No. 1 overall pick's long-term role with the franchise is murky at best.

5211983.h: Dadiet (undisclosed) will play in Thursday's Summer League game against Golden State, James L. Edwards III of The Athletic reports.
5211983.s: Dadiet appears to have been held out as a precaution Monday and will be back in the mix for Thursday's matchup. He's in line to see his first Summer League action since Saturday, when he registered 13 points, three rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block in 23 minutes against San Antonio.

5211983.h: Dadiet (undisclosed) is out for Monday's Summer League game against the Pistons, James L. Edwards III of The Athletic reports.
5211983.s: This is likely a maintenance day for Dadiet. His next chance to play comes Thursday against the Warriors.

5211983.h: Dadiet appeared in 29 regular-season games in 2025-26, averaging 1.7 points and 0.9 rebounds while shooting 33.3 percent from the field in 4.7 minutes per showing.
5211983.s: While Dadiet appeared in 11 more games than he did as a rookie, he averaged fewer minutes per game and scored in double figures just twice. However, the 20-year-old swingman took a step forward in the G League compared to 2024-25. Over 19 appearances with the Westchester Knicks this season, he averaged 22.2 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.1 steals across 34.6 minutes per contest.

5214640.h: Jakucionis (rest) didn't play in Saturday's 96-94 Summer League win over Philadelphia.
5214640.s: Jakucionis took a seat for both of Milwaukee's final three Summer League outings. Over two Las Vegas Summer League contests, he averaged 9.0 points, 5.0 assists, 2.5 steals and 1.5 rebounds in 21.7 minutes per tilt.

5214640.h: Jakucionis (rest) isn't playing in Wednesday's Summer League contest against the Hornets, according to Eric Nehm of The Athletic.
5214640.s: Jakucionis is expected to operate as a backup option in the Bucks backcourt after he was acquired in the trade that sent Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) to Miami. The second-year guard will aim to return to the hardwood when the Bucks play their next Summer League game over the weekend. Jakucionis is averaging 9.0 points and 5.0 assists per game in two Summer League appearances.

5214640.h: Jakucionis was traded to Milwaukee on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Also included, the Bucks will receive Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez, Tyler Herro and picks, while the Heat will acquire Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis.
5214640.s: Jakucionis spent his inaugural season with the Heat. While the 2025 No. 20 overall pick wasn't a consistent producer, he showed flashes of promise by averaging 8.4 points, 4.2 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 0.3 blocks, 0.8 steals and 45.8 percent shooting from deep across 24.3 minutes in 12 regular-season starts. Jakucionis is viewed as a young, up-and-coming player, though he may be a few years away from earning a stable…

5217746.h: Hansen (illness) is available for Monday's Summer League game against Minnesota.
5217746.s: Hansen will return Monday, marking his second appearance of the Las Vegas Summer League. The 21-year-old last played in Friday's 81-79 loss to Phoenix, finishing with 12 points, nine rebounds and four assists across 26 minutes.

5217746.h: Hansen (illness) has been ruled out for Sunday's Summer League game against the Magic.
5217746.s: Hansen is under the weather and will miss the front end of this back-to-back set. The big man's next chance to play will come Monday against the Timberwolves.

5217746.h: Hansen is expected to play in the 2026 NBA Summer League, Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland reports.
5217746.s: Hansen will join Portland's Summer League squad after he is done playing for China in the FIBA World Cup qualifier. The 2025 No. 16 overall pick is coming off a quiet inaugural campaign during which he averaged 2.2 points, 1.5 rebounds, 0.5 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.1 steals across 7.0 minutes in 43 regular-season appearances. With the Trail Blazers in need of depth behind Donovan Clingan, Hansen will need to…

5238230.h: Johnson (rest) is likely to revert to a bench role to open 2026-27 after finishing last season as a starter.
5238230.s: The Wizards are set to send out a new starting lineup this year, now headlined by veteran stars Trae Young (quad) and Anthony Davis (finger) as well as rookie No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa, and they're also set to get Kyshawn George and Alex Sarr (foot) back in the fold. Washington does have a rather thin backcourt behind Young and George, however, so both Johnson and Bub Carrington should remain involved to a…

5238230.h: Johnson (rest) has been shut down for the remainder of the Las Vegas Summer League, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
5238230.s: Johnson appeared in just one game for the Wizards this summer, posting 26 points (11-20 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal across 28 minutes in Thursday's win over Utah. AJ Dybantsa and Will Riley have also been shut down for the remainder of Summer League.

5238230.h: Johnson (undisclosed) won't play in Sunday's Summer League game against the Kings, Joshua Valdez of ClutchPoints.com reports.
5238230.s: The Wizards may have seen enough from Johnson this summer after he dropped 26 points in Thursday's win over Utah. His next chance to play will come Tuesday against Chicago.

5238230.h: The arrival of AJ Dybantsa, who was the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, creates additional competition on the wing, though Johnson (foot) should still maintain a decent role in Washington's young core.
5238230.s: The 2025 lottery pick showed flashes as a scorer during his rookie season and figures to remain an important perimeter option alongside Dybantsa, Kyshawn George and Bilal Coulibaly. While touches may become harder to find on a deeper roster, especially with Trae Young around, Johnson's long-term outlook remains strong as the Wizards continue building around multiple young wings.

5239561.h: Richardson has some obstacles to climb in order to seize an Opening Night role.
5239561.s: The 2025 first-rounder was not a big part of Orlando's rotation in his rookie season, averaging 10.9 minutes per game over 54 regular-season appearances. With Anthony Black primed to serve as the Magic's sixth man off the bench, Richardson is left to compete with the likes of Jamal Cain, Noah Penda and Jevon Carter for reserve minutes this season.

5239561.h: Richardson (rest) won't play in Saturday's Summer League game against the Celtics, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
5239561.s: Richardson will sit out Orlando's Summer League finale for rest purposes. Over three Las Vegas Summer League appearances, the 20-year-old guard averaged 18.3 points, 4.7 assists, 3.7 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 30.1 minutes per game.

5239561.h: Richardson (undisclosed) will miss Sunday's Las Vegas Summer League game against the Trail Blazers.
5239561.s: Richardson will sit out the second leg of a Summer League back-to-back set, but he should return for Wednesday's meeting with the 76ers. TyTy Washington will draw the start in Richardson's absence Sunday, and there should be more minutes available for Keon Johnson.

5254165.h: Head coach Ty Lue said Wednesday the Clippers are going to give Wagler a lot of on-ball opportunities, per Joey Linn of SI.com.
5254165.s: With Brandon Ingram (Achilles) sidelined to begin the season, Los Angeles is already short on proven playmakers beyond Darius Garland. Bradley Beal (knee) appears ticketed for a reserve role, meaning Wagler has a chance to be the team's second scoring option behind Garland while Ingram is sidelined.

5254165.h: Wagler (rest) has been ruled out for Wednesday's Summer League game against the Wizards, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
5254165.s: Wagler will get a break after playing in each of the Clippers' first three games of the Summer League, and his next chance to play is Friday against the Timberwolves. The No. 5 overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, Wagler figures to start alongside Darius Garland in the backcourt for the 2026-27 season. Wagler averaged 17.9 points, 5.0 rebounds and 4.3 assists over 33.9 minutes per game last year with Illinois.

5254165.h: Wagler was selected by the Clippers with the No. 5 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
5254165.s: Wagler caps off a meteoric rise over the past year, transitioning from an unheralded four-star recruit into a top-5 selection after a spectacular freshman season at Illinois. The 19-year-old guard was the centerpiece of the Fighting Illini offense, taking home Big Ten Freshman of the Year and Jerry West Award honors while averaging 17.9 points, 5.0 rebounds and 4.3 assists per contest. A creative 6-foot-6 playmaker…

5279130.h: Nets general manager Sean Marks said Sunday that Traore (knee) is healthy and ready to participate in training camp, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
5279130.s: Traore underwent a procedure on his right knee in June after dealing with soreness during the 2025-26 campaign, causing him to miss Summer League. The second-year guard appears to have completed his recovery on schedule and should enter camp with mild restrictions as he competes for a role in Brooklyn's crowded backcourt.

5279130.h: Brooklyn general manager Sean Marks announced Monday that Traore underwent right knee surgery and won't play in Summer League, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
5279130.s: Although Traore won't play in Summer League, he's expected to be 100 percent by training camp. During his rookie campaign, Traore averaged 8.9 points, 3.8 assists and 1.8 rebounds while shooting 38.0 percent from the field in 22.2 minutes per showing across 56 regular-season games (31 starts).

5279130.h: Traore (illness) has another obstacle for minutes in the backcourt after the Nets chose Mikel Brown with the No. 6 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
5279130.s: Traore had a hard time sticking with Brooklyn in the early stages of 2025-26, spending most of his time with the G League's Long Island Nets. His role changed drastically during the second half of the year, however, as the 2025 first-rounder started on effectively a full-time basis from Jan. 29 onward. The Nets have a logjam in the backcourt, featuring Egor Demin (foot), Drake Powell and Ben Saraf along with Brown,…

5281370.h: Steinbach was selected by the Hornets with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
5281370.s: Steinbach played professionally in Germany before heading to Washington for his lone college season. Over 30 appearances for the Huskies, the 20-year-old big man averaged 18.5 points, 11.8 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.2 blocks and 1.1 steals while shooting 57.7 percent from the field and 34.0 percent from downtown in 34.6 minutes per contest. Steinbach will now join a team that has the potential to make waves in the…

5289900.h: Diawara said he's completely healthy after undergoing surgery for a minor finger injury this summer, Steve Popper of Newsday reports Saturday.
5289900.s: Diawara missed the Knicks' final three Las Vegas Summer League games due to the finger injury, though he should be ready to go for Monday's preseason opener against the 76ers. The 21-year-old forward appeared in 69 regular-season games (seven starts) in his rookie season, averaging 3.6 points and 1.4 rebounds in 9.2 minutes per contest.

5289900.h: Diawara (finger) didn't play in Friday's 110-88 Summer League loss to the Mavericks.
5289900.s: The severity of the finger injury is unknown, though it kept Diawara from playing in New York's final three Las Vegas Summer League outings. Over two outings in Las Vegas this summer, he averaged 3.5 points and 5.5 rebounds in 24.7 minutes per tilt.

5289900.h: Diawara (finger) is out for Thursday's Summer League game against Golden State, James L. Edwards III of The Athletic reports.
5289900.s: Diawara will remain sidelined for Thursday's clash while tending to a finger issue. His next opportunity to play will arrive Friday against Dallas.

5289900.h: Diawara (finger) is out for Monday's Summer League game against the Pistons, per James L. Edwards III of The Athletic.
5289900.s: Diawara is nursing a finger injury and can be deemed day-to-day going forward. His next chance to play comes Thursday against the Warriors.

5289900.h: Diawara agreed to a multi-year contract with the Knicks on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
5289900.s: Charania reports that the deal is expected to be worth at least $10 million, though the contract details have not yet been disclosed. Diawara saw an inconsistent role during his rookie campaign, stepping up when injuries arose. Across 69 regular-season games (seven starts), the 21-year-old forward averaged 3.6 points and 1.4 rebounds in 9.2 minutes per tilt.
